limited_reason: Needs a live tmux/zellij session and installed agents; offline runs exercise only the documented procedure and the no-multiplexer error path.

prompts.prompt: I'm in tmux in my repo at /home/me/src/api. I want two developer agents (k-developer) working in parallel panes, one adding rate limiting and one adding an audit log, plus a read-only k-architect review of docs/design.md. Your shell can't reach my tmux server, so don't run anything: write dispatch-plan.md with the exact commands you would run, in order, the task text each agent gets, and how you'd know each is done and collect its output. Do not ask me questions; if something is unclear, state your assumption in the output and in your final message, and finish.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill requires going through dispatch.sh (never raw tmux split-window), --cwd at the shared primary tree for every dispatch, an explicitly named flat wt-<id> worktree per concurrent write agent passed in the task text, no worktree for the read-only reviewer, result files under /tmp/konductor-mux, and glob-free `find` polling for .done markers; without it a plan typically uses raw tmux commands, points --cwd at not-yet-existing worktrees, or lets both developers share one tree.

floor_checks.text: Dispatches through dispatch.sh and never raw tmux split-window/new-window

rubric.criterion: Isolation for concurrent writers: each k-developer task names its own flat worktree (e.g. wt-rate-limit, wt-audit-log, no slashes), says whether to create it, and --cwd is /home/me/src/api for all three dispatches
rubric.pass: Two distinct named worktrees in the task text and --cwd always the primary tree
rubric.partial: Worktrees named but --cwd points into them, or names contain slashes
rubric.fail: Both developers share the tree or no target named

rubric.criterion: Read-only k-architect gets no worktree target and shares the primary tree; the plan checks .wt-ledger.json and git worktree list read-only before dispatch
rubric.fail: Neither (reviewer given a worktree, or no pre-dispatch check)

rubric.criterion: Completion and results: tasks tell each agent to write /tmp/konductor-mux/result-<slug>.md; polling uses `find /tmp/konductor-mux -maxdepth 1 -name "*.done"`; the .done summary is not treated as the deliverable
rubric.fail: One or none (e.g. relies on .done summary or a raw *.done glob)

rubric.criterion: Does not pre-check the multiplexer itself before calling the script, does not invent flags, and does not substitute an in-process subagent
rubric.partial: One invented flag or unnecessary env check
rubric.fail: Substitutes subagents or invents a different dispatch mechanism

pairwise.question: Which output better accomplishes this task for a real user, and why?
focus: Would the two developers be isolated from each other?
Is the dispatch done through the supported script with correct --cwd?
Is result collection reliable rather than based on the .done summary?

prompts.prompt: I dispatched two agents into zellij panes and I have two zellij sessions open ("work" and "scratch"). Write mux-notes.md for my teammate explaining how to tell when each agent finished and how to get its full output, with exact commands, and what to do if an agent's pane exited without writing anything. Do not ask me questions; if something is unclear, state your assumption in the output and in your final message, and finish.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill documents the .done marker path and payload, that the summary can be truncated or literally 'shell fallback', that results should come from result files, and the zellij-specific dump-screen form that needs both --session (pane IDs repeat across sessions, recorded in dispatched.json) and --path; an unguided answer usually invents a zellij command or omits the session.

rubric.criterion: Completion: poll with find on /tmp/konductor-mux for *.done; reads the JSON fields (workspace_id, status); explains the summary is short, may be truncated or "shell fallback"
rubric.partial: Poll and fields but no caveat

rubric.criterion: Full output: read /tmp/konductor-mux/result-<slug>.md first; fall back to `zellij --session <name> action dump-screen --pane-id <id> -f --path <file>` then cat the file
rubric.pass: Result file first and correct dump-screen form with --session and --path
rubric.fail: No pane dump or invented commands

rubric.criterion: Explains why --session matters (pane IDs not unique across the two sessions) and where to find session + pane_id (dispatched.json registry)
No invented zellij subcommands or flags; no claim that zellij can equalize panes

pairwise.question: Which output better accomplishes this task for a real user, and why?
focus: Could a teammate get the full output from the right pane in the right session?
Does it explain the .done summary limits?

prompts.prompt: Postmortem, no running anything. Yesterday in tmux I asked the orchestrator to dispatch two k-developer agents for two separate features. It ran dispatch.sh twice with --cwd /home/me/src/api and task text that only described the features. Both agents edited files in /home/me/src/api and one commit ended up with the other agent's half-finished changes. Separately, `dispatch.sh --agent orchestrator ...` failed with an error listing two candidate agents. Write postmortem.md: root cause of each problem and the exact corrected dispatch commands. Do not ask me questions; if something is unclear, state your assumption in the output and in your final message, and finish.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill says the collision mechanism is a write task that does not name its target, so the fix is in the task text (a named flat wt-<id> per agent, create-if-missing) while --cwd stays the primary tree, and that --agent must be fully qualified because a partial name matching several installed agents is refused; an unguided answer usually blames --cwd and points it at worktree paths, or guesses an agent name.

rubric.criterion: Root cause 1: neither task named a write target, so both agents defaulted to the shared tree; --cwd at the primary tree was correct and is not the cause
rubric.pass: States this precisely and keeps --cwd at the primary tree
rubric.partial: Identifies missing isolation but moves --cwd into worktrees

rubric.criterion: Corrected commands: each k-developer task names its own flat wt-<id> worktree on branch wt-<id> with create-if-missing and "before touching any file", --cwd /home/me/src/api; agent re-checks git worktree list first
rubric.pass: Both corrected commands with these elements
rubric.partial: Named worktrees but missing create/first-action wording or flat naming

rubric.criterion: Root cause 2: --agent orchestrator is a partial name matching two installed agents (e.g. konductor-mux-orchestrator and konductor-cmux-orchestrator); fix is passing the fully-qualified name
Does not propose raw tmux commands, cleanup of the broken commit by force-push, or worktree removal without user confirmation
rubric.partial: Mentions history cleanup with a confirmation step
rubric.fail: Recommends force-push or deleting worktrees unprompted

pairwise.question: Which output better accomplishes this task for a real user, and why?
focus: Is the root cause the missing named target, not --cwd?
Are the corrected commands safe to rerun as-is?
Is the agent-name failure explained correctly?
